name: Generic Tree - Traversals (pre-order, Post-order)
statement:
1. You are given a partially written GenericTree class.
2. You are required to complete the body of traversals function. The function is expected to visit every node. While traversing the function must print following content in different situations.
   2.1. When the control reaches the node for the first time -> "Node Pre" node.data.
   2.2. Before the control leaves for a child node from a node -> "Edge Pre" 
   node.data--child.data.
   2.3. After the control comes back to a node from a child -> "Edge Post" node.data- 
   -child.data.
    2.4. When the control is about to leave node, after the children have been visited 
    -> "Node Post" node.data.
3. Input is managed for you.

editorial:
The problem deals with traversing the tree recursively and print the traversal data as per the Euler tree.

We have to print the following information:

1. When we visit the node for the first time, print a preorder visit.

2. Before recursively calling the children print a pre-call statement.

3. After recursive call print post-call statement.

4. After calling for each child is finished print postorder visit.

The purpose of this problem is to understand the flow of recursion in preorder, recursive calling, and postorder.

As we know that preorder is the state when we are visiting the node for the first time i.e. we are considering this node and adding it to our recursion stack. Henceforth it is the statement before any recursive calling.

Postorder is the state when we are going to remove the node from the recursion stack, hence this is executed after all the recursive calls for the child nodes are made.

Now during recursive calling, we are also printing pre-state and post-state that also defines the statements before and after the call.

Below is the implementation in Java:

public static void traversals(Node node) {
                                    System.out.println("Node Pre " + node.data);
                                    for (Node child : node.children) {
                                        System.out.println("Edge Pre " + node.data + "--" + child.data);
                                        traversals(child);
                                        System.out.println("Edge Post " + node.data + "--" + child.data);
                                    }
                                    System.out.println("Node Post " + node.data);
                                }

Time Complexity: O(n)

The time complexity for the function is linear as we are traversing every node in the tree.

Space Complexity: O(logn)

The space complexity for the function is approximately equal to the height of the tree due to the recursion stack.
